transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Uh… I guess the main reason is work. I keep getting up from my desk during the day, even when I know I’m supposed to stay there and finish reviewing claims. It’s been causing enough of a problem that I thought I should come in.
Did you notice this kind of restlessness and trouble staying seated going back to when you were a child, or is this something that started more recently as an adult?

Yeah… I think it goes back. I don’t know about the staying seated part exactly, but in elementary school teachers would write stuff like I was bright, but I’d lose worksheets, miss instructions, and needed reminders to finish my classwork. So it wasn’t totally new.
Have you noticed feeling unusually drowsy or fighting to stay awake during the day, even after what seems like a full night's sleep?
Not really, no. I mean, I get tired sometimes like anyone, but I don’t usually feel like I’m fighting to stay awake after sleeping.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things—like work, health, or family—more days than not, even when there's no clear reason to worry?
Um… not really, I don’t think so. I mean, I worry about work stuff when it’s going badly, but I wouldn’t say it’s constant or about everything.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others, blurting out answers, or acting impulsively without thinking things through?
Not really. I mean, I might talk over someone once in a while, but I don’t think that’s a big pattern for me. I usually try to hold back.
Outside of work, do you also notice trouble staying focused on tasks—like reading, paying bills, or conversations—where your mind wanders or you lose track of what you were doing?

Yeah… that does happen. If I’m reading something and people nearby start talking, or I suddenly remember some random errand, I kind of lose the thread. Then I have to go back and reread the same part a few times.
Do you notice these same kinds of concentration or organization problems affecting things at home, like managing bills, chores, or personal relationships?

Yeah… mostly with work-type stuff, honestly. I forget simple follow-ups more than I’d like to admit, like calling a claimant back or updating a diary note. Sometimes I’ll mean to send a form earlier in the day and then realize later I never did.

Do you notice similar forgetfulness or losing track of things in your personal life at home—like forgetting to pay a bill, missing an appointment, or losing track of a conversation with your partner or friends?
Mostly I notice it with work stuff, honestly. Like I’ll mean to call someone back or update a note, or send a form, and then later I realize I just… didn’t do it. At home, I’m not as sure.
Do you notice yourself feeling restless or needing to get up and move around in other situations outside of work—like during meals, watching TV, or sitting through a movie?

Not as much outside of work, I guess. The main thing is at my desk… I keep getting up from my workstation during the day, even when I know I’m supposed to just stay there and finish the claim reviews.
Do you notice yourself losing track of conversations, forgetting things people told you, or missing social plans with friends or family?

I mean… not really sure with friends or family. The thing I notice more is work follow-ups — like I’ll forget to return a claimant’s call, or I meant to update a diary note or send a form earlier, and then I realize later I didn’t.
Has a partner, friend, or family member ever told you that you seem distracted, zone out, or forget things they've said during conversations?

Not really in those words. I guess it happens more when I’m trying to read something for a claim—if people nearby start talking about another case, or I suddenly remember some random errand, I kind of lose the thread and have to reread the same part a few times.
How long have these current problems with getting up from your desk and losing focus at work been going on—weeks, months, or longer?
It’s been longer than weeks… probably since the department reorganization, so maybe around 15 months now.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports childhood-onset attentional difficulties (documented by teachers noting he lost worksheets, missed instructions, needed reminders) alongside current impairing symptoms of inattention (losing track while reading, forgetting to complete follow-up tasks/forms/calls) and motor restlessness (repeatedly getting up from his desk despite needing to stay seated). This pattern of longstanding inattentive and hyperactive symptoms causing functional impairment supports a diagnosis of Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, combined presentation (ICD-10 F90.0, Disturbance of Activity and Attention).
